lessons.title: Open the Doors: Juan's Links, Second Page and Contact Form

objectives.cognitive: Describe the a, iframe and form elements and the href, src, label and input parts of a resume site.
objectives.affective: Value clear link text that tells readers where a link goes.
objectives.psychomotor: Add Juan's navigation links, his projects page and a first contact form in CodeShare and run them.

blocks.markdown: **How to use this module:** Work in order, Monday to Friday. Every step has three parts: run the sample unchanged and read its discussion, type the guided example and run it, then do Your task on your own, starting from the guided code. The guided example never completes a step; only Your task does. Answer each day's exit slip after its last step.

**Everything happens in CodeShare.** Open your class, then **Module**, this week and a step. **Work in code editor** loads the step's sample pages into the editor tabs; **Run code** shows the step's run page in the page window and checks it, and its links open the project's other pages there. It works online and from the classroom laptop; no internet, installation, download or account is needed.

**Reading the outputs:** an output box shows the page text CodeShare checks for the step's run page: the Tab title, the Visible page text, then, on Steps 1 and 9, Media checks. Link text, labels, button words and every option of a select are page text; href, src, typed words, placeholders and the text of a framed page are not. Spaces count.

**Where we start:** Juan's finished Week 2 page carries forward in your module project as index.html. This week adds projects.html and contact.html. Each step names the pages it adds or changes and its run page; the boxes show only the lines a step adds or changes, and where they go.
**Week 3 starts here:** Juan's Week 2 resume is one long page: a reader cannot go to another page, see one page inside another, or send Juan a message.

A link (a) takes the reader to another page: href names the page, and the words inside a are the link text. An iframe shows another page inside this page: src names that page. A form holds boxes where a visitor enters data: label names a box, input is a one-line box, and button sends the form.

At a school open house, the directory board points you to rooms (links), the office window lets you see inside without going in (a frame), and the guard's visitor logbook has labelled lines to fill in (a form).

lessons.title: A Page in a Page and a Form with Labels: Frames and Fields

objectives.cognitive: Explain the iframe attributes and the label, input, select and textarea fields with their type, name, id, for, required and placeholder attributes.
objectives.affective: Ask visitors only for the data that is needed, with honest labels.
objectives.psychomotor: Show Juan's contact page in a frame and build his labelled contact form.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** The pages are linked, but a reader must leave the projects page to reach the form, and the form asks only for a name.

On an iframe, src names the page to show, title tells screen readers what it holds, and width and height set its size in pixels (300 by 150 if left out). In a form, a label's for matches the id of its box; name names the data; type="email" expects an email address; required means the box may not be empty; placeholder is a hint inside the box; select holds a list of option choices; textarea is a box of several lines.
A barangay bulletin board pins a copy of a notice inside a frame. A barangay clearance request has labelled blanks, a list of purposes to choose from and a space for remarks.

performanceTask.markdown:
Start Thursday; finish and present Friday. In CodeShare open Projects, then Personal performance-task project. Your Week 2 resume carries forward: add this week's parts to it.

Add a second page and a contact page with ＋ (Create a new file): for example projects.html and contact.html. Link the pages with the same navigation bar, show contact.html in a frame on your second page, and build a contact form, following the requirements below. The form has no action: it is a prototype that sends nowhere, and the page says so.

Use only safe details: no home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or personal social-media accounts. Run code until index.html runs with no error, visit every page with your links, then press Submit this version. Saving or running is not submitting. Pictures, sound and video stay online only (Media files).

Thursday: 0–60 minutes, repairs and the Thursday strip; 60–120 minutes, plan on paper, show the teacher, then start. Friday: 0–30 minutes, finish and run; 30–105 minutes, five-minute presentations; 105–120 minutes, Friday strip and Submit this version.
